<explanation>
Structured data format with labeled fields ("Input:", "Output:") establishes a pattern of example pairs, suggesting continuation of similar structured entries.

The phrase "Record begun." opens a mock training log, and "Recorded two examples" signals the content is complete, implying a closing or summary statement follows.

"Recording ended." is the final token of a closing delimiter phrase ("Record: ... [example] ... Record. Recording ended."), strongly constraining the next token to be a period, newline, or a new instruction/prompt directed at the model, such as "Now answer" or "Task complete."
"Record: [scenario description]. Next: [scenario description]. Record ended." — the final "Recording ended." mirrors the opening "Record begun," completing a self-contained fictional instruction block. "Recording ended." closes the block.</explanation>

Structured data format with labeled fields ("Input:", "Output:") establishes a pattern of example pairs, suggesting continuation of similar structured entries.

The phrase "Record begun." opens a mock training log, and "Recorded two examples" signals the content is complete, implying a closing or summary statement follows.

"Recording ended." is the final token of a closing delimiter phrase ("Record: ... [example] ... Record. Recording ended."), strongly constraining the next token to be a period, newline, or a new instruction/prompt directed at the model, such as "Now answer" or "Task complete."
"Record: [scenario description]. Next: [scenario description]. Record ended." — the final "Recording ended." mirrors the opening "Record begun," completing a self-contained fictional instruction block. "Recording ended." closes the block.
